title: Detect + mitigate imaging timeouts for specific SKU/region (fallback mirror / prewarm)
creator: Vanessa Ortiz
project: Provision-to-ready automation sprint (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
description:
Context
During Week 1/2 pilot runs of the provision-to-ready pipeline, we saw a recurring failure mode: Imaging stage occasionally exceeds the max stage duration and times out for a specific combination of region + GPU SKU. This blocks end-to-end automation and creates noisy manual handoffs.

Observed behavior
- Stage: Imaging (after Provisioning, before Bootstrapping)
- Symptom: timeout while pulling / applying golden image artifacts (node bootstrap never reaches "image applied" marker)
- Correlation: spikes in a single region (EU) and mostly on one newer SKU family (H100 class nodes); other regions/SKUs generally fine.
- Operator-facing symptom: provisioning run shows "Imaging" stuck until watchdog cancels; retry sometimes succeeds.

Hypothesis (from logs + operator notes)
- Primary: image artifact mirror path intermittently slow/unreachable from that region (e.g., transient egress/peering issues, throttling, or mirror saturation).
- Secondary: cold-cache behavior when a new SKU lands in a region; first nodes pay the full download/extract cost and exceed stage budget.

Goal
Add deterministic detection + automatic mitigation so imaging becomes (a) observable with a clear cause and (b) resilient via fallback routes.

Non-goals
- Redesign of the golden image build pipeline (handled in ENG-2744).
- Changing vendor-level network architecture.

Proposed approach
1) Detection (fast-fail)
- Before starting the full imaging apply, run a lightweight mirror reachability + throughput probe:
  - DNS resolve + TLS handshake
  - HEAD/GET of a small known object (or manifest)
  - Optional: short bounded download test (e.g., 10–50MB) to estimate throughput
- If probe fails or is below threshold for N seconds, record a structured event and switch to fallback.

2) Fallback options
- Mirror fallback:
  - Primary mirror (regional) -> secondary mirror (alternate region / alternate CDN endpoint)
  - Order should be deterministic and logged, including which endpoint was used.
- Prewarm option:
  - For the problematic region/SKU, prewarm the image artifacts on a per-AZ cache/bastion or node-local cache if available.
  - Prewarm is triggered only when we detect cold start or repeated imaging failures in the last X hours.

3) Retry semantics
- Imaging step should use bounded retry/backoff and be cancel-safe.
- Retries must not leave the node in an ambiguous partially-imaged state; on retry we should:
  - re-validate current image version marker
  - if marker absent/old, re-apply; if marker present and matches intended version, short-circuit

4) Metrics + events
Emit the following (names indicative; final per observability naming conventions):
- provisioning_stage_duration_seconds{stage="imaging", region, sku}
- imaging_mirror_probe_latency_ms{mirror, region}
- imaging_mirror_probe_result{mirror, region} = success|dns_fail|tls_fail|timeout|slow
- imaging_fallback_used{from, to, region, sku} (counter)
- imaging_artifact_bytes_downloaded (histogram)
- imaging_error_category = mirror_unreachable|mirror_slow|checksum_fail|apply_failed|unknown

Acceptance criteria
- If primary mirror is unavailable/slow, imaging automatically switches to fallback mirror and proceeds (no operator intervention) for >= 80% of previously failing cases.
- When imaging fails, operators see an explicit error category and the chosen mirror endpoint in the run status.
- Stage timing dashboard shows reduced p95 imaging duration for the affected region/SKU, and reduced failure rate.
- Runbook update: documented knobs (thresholds, mirrors), how to override/force mirror for debugging, and how to tell if prewarm ran.

Implementation notes
- Fleet-provisioner: add mirror probe + endpoint selection logic at start of Imaging stage.
- Config: add optional "imageMirrors" list and "mirrorProbe" thresholds (with sane defaults) to pool config; keep escape hatch for one-off debugging (admin-only override, audited).
- Ensure the selected mirror endpoint is included in the provisioning correlation ID context so logs/events tie together.

Rollout plan
- Enable in staging first (feature flag already planned for provisioning pipeline).
- Shadow mode for 24h: run probe + log decision but do not switch mirrors (confirm signal quality).
- Then enable automatic fallback for the impacted region only.
- Expand to all regions after 1 week if no unexpected regressions.

Links
- Slack investigation thread (slow imaging): sources/slack/eng-infra/1708539011.json
- Provision-to-ready overview: sources/confluence/eng-infra/gpu-fleet-and-capacity/provision-to-ready-automation-overview.json
- Time-to-ready metrics spec: sources/confluence/eng-sre/operational-tooling/time-to-ready-metrics-and-alerting.json

Related PRs (expected)
- Retry/backoff policy groundwork: sources/github/redwood/pr-48241.json (used by imaging stage as well)

Risks / open questions
- Mirror fallback could mask underlying infra issues; ensure we still alert on elevated fallback rate.
- Need to confirm that alternate mirror location is compliant with customer data isolation expectations (note: these are base image artifacts, not customer data).
- Threshold tuning: avoid flapping between mirrors; implement stickiness per run.
comments:
2024-02-28 — Vanessa Ortiz (creator)
Creating this off the back of the EU imaging timeouts we hit twice this week. This is blocking the “hands-off” pilot. Let’s aim for: (1) detect slow mirror deterministically, (2) auto-fallback with a clear event, (3) metrics so SRE can set alerting based on fallback rate.

Assigning to Gabe since this touches fleet-provisioner imaging stage + retry semantics.
2024-02-29 — Gabe Wilson
Initial triage:
- The timeout correlates with image artifact fetch taking >25m (stage budget is 30m, leaving little room for apply).
- Logs show repeated retries on a single URL; no attempt to switch endpoints.
Plan: add a pre-flight probe and plumb a list of mirrors (primary + secondary). If probe says primary is slow/unreachable, choose secondary and record it in the provisioning run.
2024-03-01 — Victor Alvarez
Networking note: the region in question had intermittent packet loss to the artifact endpoint yesterday (not a total outage). A throughput-based probe makes sense. Please also log resolved IP + SNI so we can correlate with network events.
2024-03-04 — Aisha Bello
For observability, please emit a dedicated counter for fallback usage (by region + sku) so we can alert on sustained elevated fallback rate. Also, include failure reason categories so we can page only on “unknown”/“apply_failed” and not on transient mirror slowness.
2024-03-06 — Gabe Wilson
Implemented mirror probe + deterministic selection locally; pushing behind the provisioning feature flag. Added “sticky mirror selection” per run to avoid switching mid-flight.
Open question: do we want prewarm now or defer? I think mirror fallback gets us 80% of the win; prewarm could be follow-up if p95 still too high.
2024-03-07 — Vanessa Ortiz
Agree: ship fallback first, keep prewarm as optional path but not required to close this ticket. We can file a follow-up if imaging p95 remains above budget for cold starts.
2024-03-11 — Gabe Wilson
Staging results (shadow mode for ~24h):
- Probe flags “slow” on the primary mirror intermittently; secondary mirror consistently faster.
- No false positives seen in other regions.
Turning on real fallback for EU only next.
2024-03-14 — Rafael Mendes
Reviewed the failure modes: make sure we still surface an alert when fallback rate >X% over 1h so we don’t silently rely on secondary forever. Also please ensure cancellation works cleanly (no nodes left half-imaged).
2024-03-18 — Gabe Wilson
Rolled out fallback in staging + EU prod pilot pools under the feature flag.
Results so far:
- Previously failing runs now complete imaging via secondary mirror.
- Imaging failure rate down; primary issue now shows as “mirror_slow” with fallback_used=true.
Marking done; I’ll follow up with a separate ticket if we need prewarm to bring p95 down further.
